tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: Reads 1-10 company websites (homepage plus about/contact pages) and returns per domain: company and legal name, description, industry guess, address when published, founded year and stated employee count when published, logo, company social pages (LinkedIn, X, Facebook, Instagram, YouTube, GitHub),

tools.name: sites_using_technology
tools.description: Lists company websites that use the named technologies (all of them) or any tool in a category, e.g. Shopify, HubSpot, Klaviyo, Stripe, Intercom. Filter by country, language, niche keywords and domain rank (0-1000 authority score). Returns domain, title, country, domain rank, matched technologies, k

tools.name: company_hiring_summary
tools.description: Hiring activity of 1-5 companies from their public career boards (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday and more): open roles, roles posted in the last 7/30/90 days, change in open roles over time, new and closed roles, top functions, departments, locations and countries, seniority and remote mix, and t

tools.name: get_results
tools.description: Fetch the results of a company_profile, sites_using_technology or company_hiring_summary call that returned a run_id because it took longer than about two minutes. Returns the status while it is still running. Free: the original run is billed.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: company_hiring_summary · Private data: company_profile · Public sink: company_profile · Destructive: sites_using_technology, get_results.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: company_hiring_summary · Private data: company_profile · Public sink: company_profile · Destructive: sites_using_technology, get_results

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
